Params: This is the Helio family's old estate, not long after the completion of Atlantic Eye.
She pulls herself out of her daze and blinks slowly.

The manor's corridor is dim, and the hour hand of the clock above the door hovers just past four in the morning. A long transatlantic meeting just wrapped, and the servant who stopped her speaks with an apologetic tone.
I'm so sorry to bother you at this hour, ma'am. It's about Miss Helio.

She got into a fight with some children from the other families and got caught by the head of the family. He wasn't pleased, so he locked them up and requested their parents to come collect and punish them personally.
Miss Helio has been the only one left in confinement for a while now. Would it be too much to ask you to sign her out as her teacher first before you retire for the night?
Years ago, a young Adelyde called out to her after her medal ceremony, charging headlong into her life like a tiny storm.
Mistaking Rusalka's silence for refusal, the servant looks down, but presses on.
It's true that Lady Florence... Miss Helio's mother was brought back to the manor not long ago, but her condition really doesn't allow her to handle something like this...
Don't worry, I'll do it. I know where the confinement room is.
Sorry that you have to wait up for so long. Take tomorrow morning off. I'll make sure it gets approved and you still get paid.
She waves the relieved servant off and makes her way down to the manor's second basement level. Rounding a corner, she nods to the guard on duty and enters a sealed room bathed in harsh white light.
A girl with white hair is resting at the metal table in the center of the room. Burying her face in her arms to block out the glare, she feels years younger than she is.
As the door opens, the girl instantly looks up. Seeing who it is, she shoots out of her chair and stands at attention beside the table.
Quietly straightening her shirt, she gulps, finding she has nothing more to say.
Rusalka steps inside and takes in every bruise and scratch on her, then gives a small nod when she sees they have all been treated.
I know the family forbids fighting, so whatever punishment you see fit...
Her stomach lets out a growl right on cue, answering for her.
Figured they'd throw you in here without so much as a meal.
I'm starving too. Come on, let's find something to eat.
Rusalka is already striding off before Adelyde can blink, and she immediately scrambles after her teacher. The further they go, the more she starts to suspect they are heading the wrong way.
The dining room and the kitchen are the other way...
Feeling a little out of breath, she stops, and her eyes go wide at the manor hangar before her.
Rusalka is already standing by her airship. She tosses Adelyde a windproof helmet.
Put it on, and hold tight to my waist later. If you fall, that's on you.
The girl finds herself by a dining table, still bewildered.
The old apartment's dining area is just a nook beside the kitchen. The wooden chair creaks lightly as she sits.
Rusalka sets a glass of water in front of her, then heads into the kitchen. Opening the fridge, she squints at its contents before calling out to Adelyde.
The girl's face scrunches up. Realizing that her teacher is genuinely asking her, she speaks up quietly.
She pulls out two tomatoes and an onion, then frowns at a slightly wilted head of lettuce before tossing it in the sink anyway. A container and an assortment of jars and bottles follow.
Adelyde cranes her neck for a better look. The container seems to have ground meat inside.
Tearing open a bag of bread, Rusalka smiles at the waft of wheat.
I don't have burger buns, so hamburger steak sandwiches it is.
Wielding the kitchen knife with the same precision and efficiency she does with her weapons, she goes to work on the ingredients.
The seasoned meat gets shaped and pressed on the hot pan, frying in oil at medium heat. The sizzling sound and the smell immediately fill the room.
The lettuce is soaked in water, and the tomatoes, onion, and pickles are sliced. Spooning two dollops of sour cream from the jar, she stirs in red wine vinegar, mayo, and a dash of pepper and salt.
She does not believe in cutting corners. Even the bread gets toasted in a pan of melted butter.
She glances over to find those crystal-red eyes at the table completely fixed on the food, every trace of her distress and shame buried beneath the hunger.
For the first time, Rusalka finds it genuinely hard not to laugh.
Put as much filling as you want inside, then wrap it up in that parchment paper over there.
By the time Adelyde has wrestled her towering sandwiches into the parchment paper, her teacher is already up in the storage room yelling at her.
Adelyde springs up onto the roof with the grace of a cat.

Sprawling on the roof with half a sandwich remaining, Rusalka watches as Adelyde looks down at her own sandwich and takes a careful bite, chewing slowly before her eyes light up and she starts wolfing it down.
After tearing through the whole thing, she looks up to find Rusalka watching her with an amused smirk, and her face immediately turns red.
Rusalka shifts her posture and leans back, gazing out at the haze over the harbor in the early morning light.
The night has not fully retreated. The sky is a deep blue-gray, shrouding the world in restful silence.
Rusalka hears the crinkle of parchment paper from a satisfied Adelyde. The girl is sneaking glances at Rusalka, apparently convinced that she is being subtle about it.
Just ask. I'm not in the business of guessing.
Is this where you stay when you're not traveling or at the manor?
This is the house I grew up in.

Adelyde looks down and traces the gaps in the red roof tiles. Clotheslines criss-cross between the windows of the packed buildings here. Anyone can figure out the demographics and relationships in this neighborhood.
The food she just ate, this scene before her eyes... None of it quite fits the image of "the blade of the Helio empire."
...So they were mocking you because they saw you come back here.
The girl's lips press tight, her dissipated rage quietly rising again.
Oh, so that's why you got into that fight? To stick up for me?
Not just for you. For myself too.
I reported them for ganging up on the new recruits, and they called us...
...A stray with no manners teaching the stray nobody wanted.
Be smarter about it next time. Start a fight during evening drills, and any injuries can be written off as accidents. I'll teach you a few dirty tricks that actually work later.
As for me... I don't need you fighting my battles.

My family goes back five generations without a drop of Helio blood, and my father was just a sailor they hired. He never came back from a storm, so they enrolled me into the family academy as part of the compensation.
They wanted a poster child... proof that outsiders could be embraced by the family. Instead, they got someone who understands its ancient creed better than anyone born into it.
History doesn't remember bloodlines. It only remembers names.
Silver-white light bleeds across the horizon as the sheltering dark slowly gives way. Rusalka sits up and settles beside the white-haired girl who is lost in thought.
Will history remember my name too?
That's up to you. Worst case scenario, you get a line: "Adelyde, student of Rusalka."
She expects the girl to push back and ask why it is not "Rusalka, teacher of Adelyde."
How wonderful. We'll be on the same line.
Against the encroaching dawn, Rusalka reaches out and draws Adelyde into her arms, her cheek resting against the girl's temple, her fingers gently tracing the girl's braids.
Where her fingers touch, the small figure dissolves into foam, fading away with the retreating night.
Erasing her from your memories with your own hands just to hide from me...\nIsn't that a shame?
Erasing her from your memories with your own hands just to hide from me... Isn't that a shame?
The woman looks up, and there stands Arius, a silver-white sun made flesh.
How touching. It makes me sick.
I imagine the old, sweet person you were couldn't really have managed something so out of character as a hug.
As for violently destroying your own memories... I'd advise against that as well.
You deleted it fast enough, so I can't dig any deeper for information on her in your mind. But it also leaves your mind less stable, and that means more gaps for me to exploit.
Before you say goodbye to your true self for good, do you have any last words for the real Adelyde?
For her... I trust she'll find her way out.
After all these years of training, she'd better be able to beat me.
For you, I've only got one thing to say.
